item.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an… — Lyudmila Korobenko, Cristian Rios, Eric T. Sawyer — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
item.description: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to… — Gefei Cai, Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Exponential integrability of SLE Minkowski content
item.description: Let $0<\kappa<8$, $d=1+\kappa/8$, and $q=2/(2-d)$. Let $\mu$ be the $d$-dimensional Minkowski content measure of either chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ in $\mathbb H$ from $0$ to $\infty$ or two-sided whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ through $0$. We prove that there exist constants $c_\kappa,C_\kappa\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \mathbb E\exp\left\{c_\kappa\left(\frac{\mu(D)}{(\operatorname{diam} D)^d}\right)^q\right\}\le C_\kappa \] for every deterministic bounded Borel set $D$ of positive diameter in the corresponding domain. The exponent $q$ in this moment bound is optimal in both settings. We also show that, almost surely, $\mu(B(z,r))=O\bigl(r^d(\log(1/r))^{1/q}\bigr)$ as $r\downarrow0$… — Dapeng Zhan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
item.description: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction. — Levent Alp\"oge, Tristan Buckmaster, Matei P. Coiculescu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / Terence Tao — What's new

item.title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
item.description: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $\sigma(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $\mu(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $\mu(p)$ known as the time constant. We compute the near-critical asymptotics of the two quantities in high dimensions, showing that \begin{align*} \sigma^2(p) \asymp (p-p_c)^2 \qquad \text{ and } \qquad \mu(p) \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{p-p_c}} \end{align*} for all $p>p_c$. Our results concerning the diffusivity confirm a conjecture of Biskup (2011). We also compute the asymptotic critical… — Chenlin Gu, Tom Hutchcroft, Xiaoran Li — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
item.description: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every… — Antonio C\'ordoba, Chuhan Sun — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: CARROT: Competitive Adaptive Graph Clustering via Semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport
item.description: Deep graph clustering (DGC) has emerged as a prominent paradigm for unsupervised attributed graph clustering. However, existing methods often struggle with two practical challenges encountered in real-world applications: the number of clusters $K$ is unknown a priori, and cluster sizes are frequently highly imbalanced. Methods relying on a pre-specified $K$ may fail to recover the underlying clustering structure when $K$ is misspecified, while many approaches implicitly favor balanced partitions, hindering the discovery of minority clusters. We propose CARROT, a Competitive Adaptive gRaph clustering framework via semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport, which introduces semi-relaxed optimal… — Ching Fan Chiang, Jia-Yu Pan, Wen-Chieh Lin — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
item.description: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\to\rho\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-\rho)/(2-\rho)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $\rho=1$. — Vyacheslav Koval, Yuval Peres — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
item.description: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is… — Khalid Akhmouch, Eric Jauer — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math) / arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
item.description: We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$. The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we… — Alexander Fribergh, Alan Hammond — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
item.description: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $\pi$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $\pi$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs. — Niels Martin M{\o}ller, Andreas Savas-Halilaj, Knut Smoczyk — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
item.description: We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calder\'on--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a… — Michael Goldman, Lukas Koch, Dario Trevisan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: The Lafforgue Transform
item.description: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local… — Zhilin Luo — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Split Ends: UV Physics branches Black Hole Hair
item.description: Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs. Moreover, BHs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. This branching has profound consequences for BH physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves. — Georg Trenkler, Leonardo G. Trombetta, Alexander Vikman — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph

item.title: Prescribing finite first singular sets of mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: For any $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and any sufficiently small positive time, we construct a smooth mean curvature flow of embedded mean-convex tori whose first singularities occur precisely at those points at that time. — Jingwen Chen — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow
item.description: We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\). — Annalisa Cesaroni, Matteo Novaga — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Symmetries, conservation laws, series solutions and singularity formation for the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations in mass coordinates
item.description: Written in Lagrangian mass coordinates, the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations for a polytropic gas become a single second-order equation for the radius $r(t,m)$ of the shell enclosing mass $m$, with adiabatic index $\gamma>1$ and entropy profile $S(m)$. We determine all point symmetries of this equation. Apart from time translation there is at most one scaling, except at the critical index $\gamma=4/3$, where a scaling exists for every entropy profile; these scalings are the entropy-fixed stabilisers of the two-parameter scaling group of the non-isentropic system, and we give the exact symmetry defect when $\gamma\neq4/3$. Noether's theorem singles out the profiles… — Adnan Shamaoon — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean-Field Games
item.description: We study second order variational mean-field games with quadratic Hamiltonian. In analogy with entropic optimal transport, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and the second author recently proposed an entropy-minimization formulation of the problem, which could be interpreted as the Lagrangian counterpart of the classical Eulerian approach. We investigate the small-noise $\Gamma$-limit for the Lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation and establish $\Gamma$-convergence of second order mean-field games towards their deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into another (dynamical) proof of the convergence of the Schr\"odinger problem to optimal transport. Moreover, we study… — Alessandro Cosenza, Luca Nenna — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: On the Bourgain-Rudnick eigenfunction restriction conjecture in four dimensions
item.description: We prove a uniform upper $L^2$ bound for eigenfunctions of the four-dimensional flat torus on the compact paraboloid $\mathbb{P}^3$. The main novelty is the use of Fourier restriction estimates. We interpret spherical lattice point statistics as non-concentration inequalities of the strength needed to apply the Du--Zhang fractal restriction theorem. We apply their result on two-dimensional slices of $\mathbb{P}^3$. Further possible extensions are also discussed. — Ciprian Demeter — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity
item.description: This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), with \(\gamma>1\), and \(\lambda(\rho)=\rho\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. The central difficulty is to derive an upper bound for the density on… — Qian Li, Zhilei Liang, Zhuan Ye — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
item.description: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges… — Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Elliptic regularization for anisotropic mean curvature flow
item.description: We develop an elliptic regularization scheme for anisotropic mean curvature flow in arbitrary dimension, with general norms serving as surface tension and mobility. Starting from a non-fattening set of finite perimeter, we prove that the vertically rescaled minimizers and translating solitons converge in the Kuratowski sense to the unique generalized level-set motion, and locally in BV to the flat flow. Furthermore, by implementing a restarting and matching procedure prior to curvature identification, we establish for the limit flat flow a coupled phase-transport and surface-energy dissipation balance valid for arbitrary, possibly crystalline, anisotropies. When the surface tension is… — Carlo Alberto Antonini, Antonio De Rosa, Massimiliano Morini, Salvatore Stuvard — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
item.description: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute… — Christopher Chalhoub, Jeroen S. W. Lamb, Martin Rasmussen — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Spectral Optimal Transport for Dynamics-Aware Sign Language Generation
item.description: Sign language generation (SLG) translates spoken-language text into pose sequences that convey its meaning. Recently, flow-based models with optimal transport (OT) have become a strong SLG baseline by handling the one-to-many nature of text-to-sign. While classifier-free guidance (CFG) could be applied to further strengthen the semantic alignment theoretically, its training involves conditional and unconditional training, which may contradict the pose-space OT, thus reducing the generation quality. Under the condition dropout, one noise sample can be paired with target motions exhibiting incompatible motion dynamics, interfering with the semantic guidance when the text condition is… — Nabeela Khan, Bowen Wu, Runwu Shi, Hanlong Li, Benjamin Yen, Carlos Toshinori Ishi — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model
item.description: We prove that the shape function of planar directed last-passage percolation with general i.i.d.\ real-valued weights is differentiable on the open first quadrant, under a moment assumption of order $p''>4$ on the positive part of the weight and a nearly optimal order $p'>1$ on the negative part. Due to known results, only directions outside a percolation cone need be considered. The proof is a multiscale path-counting argument that uses the shape theorem, oriented percolation on a coarse-grained lattice, a simple change of measure in a finite region, and the van den Berg--Kesten inequality. Our Lean-formalized proof is an AI-assisted adaptation and improvement of the OpenAI proof of… — Christopher Janjigian, Firas Rassoul-Agha, Timo Sepp\"al\"ainen — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
item.description: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos. — Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
item.description: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit. We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k — Melda Akyazi-Zavadski, Nathana\"el Berestycki, Sunil Chhita — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
item.description: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture. — Fernando Ballesta-Yag\"ue, Jonathan Hickman, Hrit Roy — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
item.description: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli… — Shirshendu Ganguly, Reza Gheissari — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
item.description: Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. This allows CuOT to adapt sampling steps to the… — Andrea Testa, S{\o}ren Hauberg, Andras Gabor Kupcsik, Tamim Asfour, Leonel Rozo — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Local Reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up
item.description: We give four regularity criteria for the forced Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The first is an $\dot H^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local Reynolds number $|v|^2/(\nu|\omega|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $M(t)$ with $\int M^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. It rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. Two further $\dot H^1$ estimates use the Newton potential of $|\omega|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the Lamb vector, so that the integral of $|\omega|^2|v|^2$ cancels. The second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by… — Ali Bouzekri — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Wave interactions for the two-dimensional self-similar Euler equations of nonconvex gases
item.description: Gases with nonconvex equations of state may differ significantly from polytropic ideal gases; for example, rarefaction and sonic shocks may occur. This paper studies a 2D Riemann initial-boundary value problem for the potential flow equations with a nonconvex equation of state. We construct global-in-time self-similar solutions by analyzing eight distinct types of wave interactions, including composite waves consisting of a sonic/double-sonic shock coupled with one or two fan waves. Three main difficulties arise in studying these wave interactions: the self-similar potential flow system is of mixed type, with its type at each point determined by the local pseudo-Mach number; the sonic or… — Geng Lai, Wancheng Sheng — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data
item.description: In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. We assume that the shear viscosity $\mu$ is a positive constant, the bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)\ge0$ depends on the density, and the heat conductivity takes the form $\kappa(\theta)=\kappa_0 \theta^\alpha$ with $\kappa_0>0$. For a broad class of density-dependent bulk viscosities, we establish the global existence and large-time behavior of strong solutions for arbitrarily large initial… — Qinghao Lei, Xin Song — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE
item.description: Visual exploration is an integral step in understanding the structure of datasets. However, systematic variation between datasets collected under different conditions, known as batch effects, can obscure shared structure and complicate their joint visualization. Existing methods often rely on cross-batch nearest-neighbor relations to integrate the batches. Yet, these local correspondences can be unreliable for challenging cross-batch geometries. We propose optimal-transport t-SNE (OT-tSNE), which replaces nearest-neighbor-based matching with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled synthetic experiments demonstrated that nearest-neighbor-based methods… — Azhar Akhmetova, Edward Eichhorn, Boris Landa, Dmitry Kobak, Sebastian Damrich — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
item.description: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that… — Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Leray's Problem for the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations with Low-Regularity Data in Planar and Three-Dimensional Axisymmetric Lipschitz Domains
item.description: In this paper, we study the steady Navier-Stokes Dirichlet problem in bounded planar and three-dimensional axisymmetric domains with finitely many disjoint Lipschitz boundary components. For prescribed velocities in $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and forces in the dual of the solenoidal energy space $V=H_0^1(\operatorname{div}0,\Omega)$, we establish finite-energy solvability under the sole compatibility condition of zero total boundary flux. Individual component fluxes are subject to no smallness or sign restrictions. In three dimensions the domain and data are axisymmetric, and swirl is allowed. The result addresses the regularity of the domain and data within these two geometric classes. The… — Zhibing Zhang — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
item.description: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $\delta$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\log\delta|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $\delta$-neighborhood of an $\epsilon$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim \epsilon^{-1}|\log\delta|^{-1}$, for $\delta$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $\epsilon$. — Iqra Altaf — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
item.description: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation… — Qinyi Zhang, Duanyu Feng, Yangshuai Wang, Hao Wang — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
item.description: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $\alpha>1$. In our model, the power $\alpha$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the… — Sandro Gallo, Matthieu Jonckheere, Alejandro H. Wences — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature II: Multiplicity One

item.title: An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of turbulence (K41) predicts that the rate of kinetic energy dissipation in a turbulent flow can remain positive as viscosity tends to zero. In 2023, Bru\`e and De Lellis used quasi-self-similar mixing to construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations exhibiting anomalous dissipation. In this paper, we show that anomalous dissipation can still occur for a flow with spiral geometry in an annulus. In the horizontal plane, we wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral and then apply alternating shears. After each pair of shears, the image of the segment shares a subarc of positive length with the original spiral. We compare the vertical… — Changhong Li — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Self-similar solutions to the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane
item.description: We classify the self-similar solutions of the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$. Using hyperbolic numbers, the self-similarity condition becomes a linear ODE system, and all solutions are obtained in closed form with explicit smoothness and completeness criteria. Translating solitons occur in three causal types, and dilation--rotation solitons are governed by the discriminant $\Delta=a^2-4(b-1)$, as in the Euclidean case. When $a^2=b^2$ the translation cannot be eliminated, owing to the zero divisors of the hyperbolic numbers, and a genuinely Lorentzian class of mixed solitons arises, whose complete smooth members form a one-parameter family… — Li Ou — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
item.description: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost. — Johann Cl{\'e}ment-Cottuz, Gilles Gasso, Maxime Berar — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: On the Planar Optimal Transport Problem
item.description: We develop a complex analytic framework based on rotation of gradient graphs for the study of quadratic cost planar optimal transport with uniform densities. Using this framework we carry out the construction, characterization, and approximation of non-degenerate optimal transport maps up to the boundary. We also identify obstructions for continuous optimal transport and construct discontinuous optimal transport maps with prescribed analytic singular sets. — Arghya Rakshit, Aranya Sen — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Stability of Viscous Shock Waves of the Compressible Navier-Stokes System with Large Initial Perturbation
item.description: We show in this paper that viscous shock waves of the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations are time-asymptotically nonlinear stable with large initial perturbation. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. As far as we know, only under a class of large initial perturbations, the asymptotical stability of weak viscous shock wave was derived. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem for weak viscous shock wave. The key idea involves combining the $a$-contraction with shifts theory with a time splitting method to obtain the weighted $L^2$ estimates, which enables us… — Lan Zhang, Huijiang Zhao — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
item.description: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an… — Lo\"ic Gassmann, Ioan Manolescu, Maran Mohanarangan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
item.description: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate… — Felix M. Haehl, Moshe Rozali — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
item.description: We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $\lambda\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $\lambda_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $\lambda_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate. — Benedikt Jahnel, Lukas L\"uchtrath, Christian M\"onch — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
item.description: The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large radial initial data without swirl, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. On the disk we require the initial acceleration to have zero trace at the wall. The initial density is bounded away from zero and, in the plane, approaches a positive constant at infinity. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. Throughout the strictly dissipative range of viscosity coefficients, every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, the result applies to Marche's… — Kexin Li — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
item.description: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$)… — Dylan Forde — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
item.description: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^\alpha\cap L_t^2H_x^{\alpha+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leq\alpha<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The… — Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru Ionescu, Hao Jia, Stan Palasek — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Compactness from fractional momentum bounds and weak solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: We consider the barotropic Navier--Stokes equations on ${\mathbb R}^3$ with constant viscosities, finite mass and finite energy. For every $\gamma>1$, a local bound on the momentum $m=\rho u$ in $L^2_tH^{-1+\sigma}_x$, $\sigma>0$, gives strong local convergence of the densities under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1. For $\gamma>9/8$ we prove, uniformly along the approximations, $$ \|I_{1-\alpha}m\|_{L^2(I\times{\mathbb R}^3)}\leq C_{I,\alpha} \qquad\text{for some }\alpha>0,\quad I\Subset(0,\infty).$$ Here $I_s$ is the spatial Riesz potential. Together with tightness of the energy at spatial infinity, this gives a global finite-energy renormalized weak solution. — Yanlin Liu, Ping Zhang — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
item.description: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different… — Toshiaki Hishida, Bum Ja Jin — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
item.description: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point.
